propositions: Directory creation and first event file write to a ticket are not atomic, leaving empty stray directories when writes are interrupted between mkdir and file write, which fsck flags as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH
Both single-event and batch event writers share the vulnerable _prepare_event function that calls os.makedirs outside the write lock, before the first event file is written under the lock

Staging directory and event must be created atomically in a temporary path, then published with a single os.rename under the write lock, ensuring directory and CREATE event appear together or not at all

Temporary staging paths use dot-prefix convention (.tmp-newticket-*) already excluded by existing fsck scanners, making them invisible to both MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH checks without scanner changes

Stale staging directories from dead processes must be swept by bounded best-effort cleanup on writer start, using process stamp (host + pid-namespace + start-time) to avoid pid recycling false positives, without touching ticket directories or violating 043f non-cleanup policy
